commands.name: names
commands.description: The cloud's pool of readable cluster names. Subcommands: list, add, remove, assign, release

commands.name: add
commands.description: Add names at the end of the cloud's cluster name pool, in the given order. Names already in the pool are skipped, so the same list can be added again. A name is 1 to 12 characters, lowercase letters a to z and digits, starting with a letter, and not a word that Azure reserves (such as azure or office). Example: omnia clusters names add --file ./prod-star-wars.txt

commands.name: assign
commands.description: Give an existing cluster a name from the pool. The name replaces the cluster's current name in Omnia Cloud, which is kept as the cluster's description. It is an alias: the cluster keeps its id-based name in Azure, because Azure can't rename a cluster. Without --name the cluster gets the next free name. A pool name it held before goes back into the pool. A cluster keeps a name once it has one: assign another name to change it. For a cluster that was created with its name, assign instead restores that name in the pool and on the cluster's record, when 'omnia clusters names list' reports that they disagree. Example: omnia clusters names assign --clusterid [clusterId] --name yoda

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the cluster names of this cloud and the cluster that holds each one, and report where the pool and the clusters disagree. Example: omnia clusters names list

commands.name: release
commands.description: Put a name back into the pool when the cluster that held it no longer exists. A name normally returns by itself when its cluster is deleted. A failed creation keeps its name while an AKS cluster is left under it in Azure: delete that AKS cluster first, then release the name. A name held by an existing cluster can't be released. Example: omnia clusters names release --name yoda

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Remove a name that no cluster holds from the cloud's cluster name pool. Example: omnia clusters names remove --name jarjar

options.name: --name
options.description: (Optional) Friendly name of cluster. When the cloud has a free name in its cluster name pool (omnia clusters names list), the cluster gets that name, also as its name in Azure, and this text is kept as the cluster's description

options.name: --allow-id-name
options.description: Create the cluster with its id as its name when the cloud's cluster name pool has no free name that fits. Without this option the cluster is then not created, because a cluster can't be renamed in Azure afterwards
